change: Family-wise inference: the max-T permutation control is replaced by the Bonferroni count, and Sidak plus an uncorrected count are added as reported diagnostics
reason: The preregistration named 'max_t_permutation' as a dependence-respecting control. A preflight on 12 seeds per generator showed this control is mathematically incapable of rejecting: the maximum of a set of p-values is permutation-invariant, so permuting the observed p-values to build a null distribution for the maximum yields a null whose every draw equals the observed maximum. The control reported a family-wise rate of 0.000 for the deliberately broken generator WEAK_LCG_BROKEN, which the Holm count rejected on 12 of 12 seeds and whose T13_words test rejects on 100% of seeds. Had this shipped, the run would have reported that a blatantly broken generator shows no family-wise evidence against it, which would have inverted the audit's central finding. The substitute is the Bonferroni count, which is valid under ARBITRARY dependence and therefore needs no independence assumption about tests that share one input stream; this is strictly more appropriate than either Holm or Sidak for the dependence the audit was worried about. Sidak (which does assume independence) and the uncorrected per-seed rejection rate are reported alongside so the size of the dependence penalty is visible rather than hidden. The primary per-test statistic, the alpha of 0.01, the seed counts, the generators, the bit lengths, the positive-control gate, and the claim guards are all UNCHANGED.

change: Implementation fixes after a discarded first attempt: RandomState adapter for the MT19937 arm, and a fail-closed completeness gate
reason: The first execution attempt completed in 330 s but 260 of 1040 battery evaluations raised, all of them the MT19937 arm, and the runner still exited 0. Two defects: (1) numpy.random.RandomState exposes randint and random_sample, not the modern integers/random that the shared battery calls, so every MT19937 evaluation raised AttributeError; (2) even after adding that adapter, RandomState.randint is int32-bounded and raises 'high is out of bounds for int32' on the battery's 2**32 word draw, so 32-bit words are now assembled from two 16-bit draws and verified uniform (top-byte chi-square 255.9 on df 255). Separately the runner was FAIL-OPEN: it reported success and wrote a manifest despite a wholly missing generator arm. It now refuses to write a manifest unless every preregistered (generator, bit length) cell produced exactly the preregistered number of successful evaluations, writing an incomplete_run.json diagnostic instead. The failed attempt is preserved as RESULTS/N004_PRODUCTION_20260926_INCOMPLETE_MT19937_ARM. No preregistered scientific content changed.

change: Third discarded attempt: raw p-value rows were never written because TEST_IDS was only populated in analyze(); run now populates it and asserts the stored row count
reason: The second attempt reported 1040/1040 successful evaluations, zero errors, and a manifest claiming raw_rows_written = 24960, but the SQLite pvalues table contained 0 rows. Cause: TEST_IDS is a module-level list that only analyze() populated, so at run time zip([], pvals) inserted nothing while the counter incremented regardless. This is the second fail-open defect in this runner and the same class as the first (a manifest asserting data that was not stored). The run path now populates TEST_IDS before writing, refuses any seed-vector whose length differs from the declared test count, and after commit asserts that the pvalues table row count equals the number of values inserted AND that the number of complete seed-vectors equals the number of evaluations. The failed artifact is preserved as RESULTS/N004_PRODUCTION_20260926_V2_NO_RAW_ROWS. No scientific content changed.

reason: Two instrument-level defects were found and are corrected here without editing any historical artifact. (1) T03_runs in the shared battery applies an extra sqrt(2) to an argument that NIST SP 800-22 Rev. 1a section 2.3 defines directly in erfc units, because it routes the value through the _erfc_p helper, which converts a z-score to a two-sided tail. The p-values are therefore systematically too large: on 200 fresh G_LAB seeds at 2^18 the shared estimator gives KS p = 6.7e-06 and 0/200 rejections at alpha = 0.01, while an independently written reference implementation of the same section gives KS p = 0.847 and 1/200 on the identical streams. The stored N-004 data shows the same generator-independent pile-up in all four generators including the deliberately broken LCG (KS p as low as 3.1e-08), and T03_runs rejects at alpha = 0.01 for none of them, so it detected its own defect rather than a generator. Additionally the standard's section 2.3 step 1 applicability condition |pi - 1/2| >= 2/sqrt(n-1) is absent from the shared implementation; it requires about a four-sigma deviation in the bit balance and is met by 0 of 200 seeds, so the test is not applicable to these streams at all. Consequence: the N-004 claim that 0 of 24 tests were miscalibrated for G_LAB is wrong for T03_runs, which is ESTIMATOR_DEFECTIVE, and the recorded 'borderline/unstable' note is now explained. The N-004 family-level BATTERY_VALID verdict is NOT overturned, because it rests on the positive control being rejected at the family-wise level, which the other 23 tests supply. (2) The read-only 2D percolation audit pinned EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY.md by whole-file SHA-256, so it reported 10 errors whenever a new experiment was registered. The whole-file baseline and its 2026-09-24 manifest digest were left untouched; instead the registry's historical prefix is pinned byte-for-byte in a frozen artifact whose digest is required to equal the baseline's whole-file digest, so any edit, reordering, deletion, or prepending inside the audited region still fails closed while legitimate appends are measured and reported. The historical evidence, the shared battery module, and every N-004 stored row are unmodified.

reason: Follow-up to entry 559358ce, which established that T03_runs is defective. Two additions. (1) All five _erfc_p callers were audited, not just the one that failed. _erfc_p(z) = erfc(|z|/sqrt(2)) is the two-sided normal tail and is valid only for standardised z-scores. Exactly one caller, T03_runs, passes a quantity SP 800-22 section 2.3 already defines in erfc units. The other four (T01_monobit, T06_dft, T07_nontemplate, T15_autocorr) pass genuine z-scores and are empirically uniform at both 2^18 and 2^22, so the sqrt(2) is correct for them: KS p between 0.014 and 0.96 with mean p within 0.03 of 0.5. T07 remains a documented structural deviation from section 2.7's chi-square form, but its normal approximation is sound because the expected match count is about 57. (2) The corrected status of record for the N-004 T03_runs cell for G_LAB is UNRESOLVED_NOT_APPLICABLE_AT_THIS_RESOLUTION at both lengths, not 'calibrated'. Three variants were evaluated on identical streams: as-implemented KS p = 1.4e-05 at 2^18 and 8.8e-06 at 2^22 (non-uniform); with the spurious sqrt(2) removed, KS p = 0.343 and 0.956 (uniform), so the sqrt(2) explains the entire recorded non-uniformity; and with the standard's applicability precondition enforced, 0 of 200 seeds are scorable at either length, because the condition |pi - 1/2| >= 2/sqrt(n-1) demands a roughly four-sigma deviation in the bit balance and a fair stream deviates about 0.0008 at 2^18 against a 0.0039 threshold. Per the frozen rule, and per the N-004 preregistration's own instruction that an unresolved outcome must not be reported as agreement, the cell cannot be scored. An important limit is recorded explicitly: the extra sqrt(2) is a deterministic property of the code, provable as an exact algebraic identity, but its empirical DETECTION is resolution- and seed-dependent. With 200 seeds it was detected at 2^18 and missed at 2^22 under one seed labelling, and detected at both under another. Non-detection is never evidence of correctness, and the classification therefore rests on the identity, not on the KS test. Two fail-open defects of my own were introduced and fixed during this work and are recorded rather than hidden: the caller audit initially reported the T15 autocorrelation cell as CONFIRMED_CALIBRATED when it had measured zero p-values, because an absent measurement was being read as a pass, and the pooled key set for that cell never resolved. The audit now raises on a declared key that is not collected and classifies an unmeasurable cell as UNRESOLVED_NO_MEASUREMENT.
